correctness.rationale: The source gives all quantitative ingredients needed for a finite certificate. A length-n formula has at most n subformulas, its single-negation closure has size at most 2n, and modal depth and every explicit successor offset are at most n. The source world bound is therefore dominated by (4n)^(n+1), the standard-model transfer preserves worlds, and the source value compression gives U_n=(nN_n+1)(n+1). Encoding relevant equivalence relations, proposition valuations, and bounded constant valuations uses 2^{O(n log n)} bits, and direct semantic verification is polynomial in that encoding.
